newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-SPRINT QUEEN VOELKER EYES THIRD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-SPRINT QUEEN VOELKER EYES THIRD RECORD.

text.p: Sandra Voelker, Germany's sprint queen, aims to win a third individual gold and break her third record on Sunday when she defends her 50 metres backstroke title from the threat of a fellow German.

"It will be very exciting, because Antje Buschschulte is very fit. I am looking forward to the heats," Voelker told journalists after she clinched her second European record at the European sprints and short-course championships, pocketing her second 5,000 mark ($3,420) prize.

"It will be difficult because I have been concentrating on butterfly and crawl and the last time I swam backstroke was four or five weeks ago," said the 22-year-old, who set the European 50 backstroke record of 27.67 seconds in Sheffield on February 22, 1995.
On Saturday, Voelker, who lives and trains in Hamburg, won the 50 freestyle in 24.67, slicing 0.08 seconds from the European short-course record she shared with fellow German Franziska van Almsick.
Voelker, who now holds 14 European short-course titles, snatched van Almsick's 100 freestyle European short-course record on Friday with a time of 53.04, well ahead of van Almsick's 53.33.

Adored in Germany, 18-year-old van Almsick was not at the championships and also lost a national record in the 50 metres butterfly on Friday to Voelker, who finished second to Johanna Sjoberg of Sweden. Sjoberg set European records in both the 50 and 100 metres butterfly.
Voelker has grabbed the limelight with her success in this former east German town but shrugged off comparisons with her younger team mate.
"The media will always think I am in her shadow. That used to bother me, but it doesn't any more. She is a very talented swimmer," said Voelker.

Voelker said she had no particular desire to become more famous than her rival. "I am already well known in the streets of Hamburg and northern Germany and it's nice to be able to go to Munich and not be recognised," she said.
Voelker sprung to prominence in this summer's Atlanta Olympics, netting a silver in the 100 freestyle, a bronze in the 50 freestyle and another bronze in the four by 100 freestyle relay.
"I've trained hard and this is a result of that," she said.
Voelker said her long-term goal was to swim in the 2000 Sydney Olympics: "I would really like to be there, but it's three and a half years away and a lot can happen in that time."
But the high-school student said she had other goals in her life besides swimming.
"I don't only want to swim. I want to do other things and I am applying to start a German and media studies degree in Hamburg next year, because I'm interested in it."
